title: JMeter Web Insight Report — annotations
description: Companion file for a JMeter run: the quality gate that decides the verdict, the server asserts judged against collected server metrics, plus notes and markers the report renders. Point an editor at this schema with a "$schema" key to get completion and typo squiggles.

testNotes.description: Markdown, rendered in the Notes tab and on the Summary tab.

assertions.description: The quality gate. Only what is declared here is ever judged; everything else the report shows is data.

samplerNotes.description: Sampler name to a note, shown as an info icon beside it in the table.

assertion.description: Unknown keys are allowed on purpose. The plugin parses one specific shape and ignores anything outside it - silently, and preserving it when the report saves the file back. A schema that flagged them would put a red squiggle in your editor on the very keys the tool promises not to touch.

id.description: Unique. Names the JUnit testcase and appears in every failure message. Derived from the target and metric when omitted - and a derived name is NOT written back if the report saves the file, because it is the plugin's name and not yours.

description.description: Carried into failure messages and the report — a good place for the contract clause this rule comes from.

metric.description: Case-insensitive. Any percentile from p50 to p99.99, fractional allowed (p99.9). median is p50, p95 is p95.0. errorRate and errorCount also take a selector: errorRate:class=protocol|nonProtocol|transport, or errorCount:code=<glob>, where * is the only special character (prefix regex: for a full expression). A metric name the engine does not know makes the rule NOT_JUDGED with reason INVALID_RULE - reported and counted, never a silent pass, and never a verdict either.

enabled.description: false parks the rule without deleting it.

target.description: What the rule judges: exactly one of sampler, samplers, match or scope. None, or more than one, makes the rule NOT_JUDGED / INVALID_RULE - picking one would judge something nobody asked for.

sampler.description: One sampler, by its exact name.

match.description: Glob, where * is the only special character and everything else is literal. Prefix with regex: for a full expression.

exclude.description: Globs removed from what match selected. Read only beside match.

scope.description: The run as a whole rather than any sampler.

predicate.description: Exactly one operator. The tester writes the direction, so latency, throughput and apdex share one rule shape.

gt.description: Breach when the value is greater than this.

lt.description: Breach when the value is less than this — throughput, apdex.

serverMetrics.description: Server asserts: what the servers should look like under this load, judged against the metrics wir-collect collected over the run's window. Where the metrics come from is a wir-collect flag, never a key here. Unknown keys are carried through a save; a retired one (sources, gates, kpis, packs) is refused by name.

components.description: What is measured, by id. Every server assert names one; there is no implicit component.

environments.description: Named sets of vars for ${env.NAME} in queries. wir-collect --env picks one; defaultEnv otherwise.

defaultEnv.description: The environment used when wir-collect is given no --env. Must be one declared under environments.

requiresLoad.description: The default for every server assert: the id of a client throughput rule that must PASS or WARN for the assert to be judged.

asserts.description: The server asserts. Only what is declared here is judged.

serverComponent.description: One thing being measured. Unknown keys are carried through a save; failsBuild is retired and refused (every component can fail the build).

type.description: A built-in catalogue type, whose metrics a server assert can name, or custom: every assert on it writes its own query.

description.description: The label on the badge, the header chip and the CI/CD JSON's serverComponents[].label. The id when omitted.

match.description: A PromQL label selector, expanded into the catalogue queries' ${match} and ${andMatch} slots to narrow them to this component's instances.

serverEnvironment.description: One environment. Its vars are written into every report, so they never hold a credential.

vars.description: Name to text, read in queries as ${env.NAME}.

serverCollection.description: Run-level knobs for the collection and the judged window.

coverageFloor.description: Fraction 0..1 of the collected window a series must cover. Below it the assert is NOT_JUDGED / LOW_COVERAGE. A bad value warns and keeps the default.

excludeRampUp.description: Leave the ramp-up (wir-collect --rampup) out of the judged window.

serverAssert.description: One server assert: a component, a catalogue metric or a query of its own, a reducer and warn/fail bands. Unknown keys are carried through a save; a retired one (source, gate, assert, range, warnAt, onMissing, onLoadShortfall, loadValidity, required, scope, overlayOn, and sustainedFor, breachBudget or over outside reduce) makes it NOT_JUDGED / INVALID_RULE.

id.description: Names the JUnit testcase and every message. Derived from the component and the metric or query when omitted.

description.description: Free text, shown under the assert's name.

enabled.description: false parks the assert: DISABLED, never judged.

component.description: The id of a component declared under components.

metric.description: A catalogue metric of the component's type. It brings the query, unit, reduce and across. Write metric or query, never both.

query.description: The series to judge, written out: PromQL, or the metric text of a --csv row. Required on a custom component. May use ${env.NAME} and ${run.*}. Write metric or query, never both.

unit.description: What the collected values are in, written beside the numbers. Converts nothing. The catalogue's for a metric.

across.description: How instances fold into one number. The catalogue's for a metric, otherwise max.

requiresLoad.description: The id of a client throughput rule that must PASS or WARN for this assert to be judged; otherwise NOT_JUDGED / LOAD_NOT_ACHIEVED. Overrides the block's requiresLoad.

divideBy.description: The id of a client throughput rule over one target: the reduced number is divided by that rule's measured value, per unit of load.

pack.description: Which pack the assert came from, such as "kafka@1". Carried through a save; it changes nothing that is judged.

serverReduce.description: How a series becomes one number. Required on a query. A metric brings the catalogue's; a reduce written here replaces it whole, so it always names kind.

kind.description: max, min, avg, last, pN (0 < N < 100, nearest-rank, e.g. p95 or p99.9) or slope (least squares, per minute).

serverTolerance.description: On max and min only: one of sustainedFor or breachBudget, never both.

sustainedFor.description: The highest (lowest) level held for at least this long: 500ms, 30s, 2m, 1h. At least 1ms.

breachBudget.description: The level exceeded at most this fraction of the window: 2% is 0.02.

timelineMarker.description: Unknown keys are allowed: a marker round-trips verbatim through the report, so flagging them here would contradict what the tool does with them.

comparisonThresholds.description: What counts as a regression on the Compare tab. Percentages, except errorRateChange which is in points. Unknown keys are allowed and round-trip verbatim.
